heading: Free PDF Compressor Online
introduction:
PDF files are commonly used for business documents, reports, forms, manuals, presentations, and study materials. They are easy to open on different devices and help keep document layouts consistent. However, some PDF files contain extra document information that may not be necessary for everyday use.

A large PDF can be inconvenient to email, upload to a website, or share through an online form. A PDF compressor can help optimize a document and check whether its file size can be reduced.

File Compresser provides an online PDF Compressor that processes supported PDF files in your browser. The tool performs a structural rewrite and removes selected metadata when it is safe to do so. You can then compare the resulting file size and download the processed document.

sections.heading: Try a structural rewrite
sections.body: Add an unsigned, unencrypted PDF within the 50 MB limit. A rewritten candidate is parsed again and its page count checked. If it is not smaller, the original is retained with 0% reduction. This is a size optimizer, not a guarantee that metadata has been sanitized.

sections.heading: Know when another approach is needed
sections.body: Large scanned PDFs often need image or scan-resolution changes for a substantial reduction. Those operations are not offered here. The optimizer does not perform OCR, remove passwords or promise a particular percentage saving.

sections.heading: Inspect the document before keeping it
sections.body: Open the download in your PDF reader and review pages, forms, links and appearance. Detected digitally signed and encrypted PDFs are refused. Keep the original because a successful parse and matching page count do not prove every document feature is unchanged.
